title: Life with wisdom brings joy, lasting wealth and good renown
speaker: The first-person royal wisdom narrator
note: Declarative sayings on wisdom's benefits continuing AUD-26-8-5 (8:5–9); could instead extend it. 8:10–15 are first-person expectations.

title: Know that wisdom is God's gift, and ask Him for it
speaker: The first-person royal wisdom narrator
note: States a maxim: knowing whose gift wisdom is is itself understanding; leads into the prayer. Cf. James 1:5 (A037).

title: Solomon recalls God making him king and ordering the temple built
speaker: God, recalled by Solomon in prayer
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Same recalled charge as Solomon's temple prayer in 1 Kings 8:19; link as Additional Scripture. Petitions of ch. 9 are out of scope.

title: Without God's wisdom even a perfect person counts for nothing
speaker: Solomon, in prayer
note: Maxim inside the prayer; the petitions are out of scope. The catalogue records a similar in-prayer maxim at 12:19.

title: Passing wisdom by brings harm; wisdom rescues those who serve her
speaker: The wisdom writer
note: Lesson drawn from the Sodom example; the rest of chapter 10 retells history and needs no record.

title: Devotion to God is stronger than everything
speaker: The wisdom writer
note: Lesson stated within the Jacob retelling ('so that he might know').

title: One is punished by the very things by which one sins
speaker: The wisdom writer
note: Governing maxim of chs. 11–19, restated at 12:23, 12:27 and 16:1; counterpart principle at 11:5.

title: God's gradual judgment gives room for repentance and teaches kindness
speaker: The wisdom writer, addressing God
note: Not contiguous with the record (12:17–22): God's sparing of the Canaanites is the example behind 12:19's lesson; 12:20 restates it.

title: Heed light rebukes before a judgment worthy of God comes
speaker: The wisdom writer
note: General principle stated in the retelling; 12:23 and 12:27 restate the 11:16 maxim.

title: Wretched are those who hope in lifeless, man-made gods
speaker: The wisdom writer
note: Woe; the woodcarver satire in 13:11–19 illustrates it (cf. Isaiah 44:9–20); link those verses as context.

title: The ungodly and their ungodliness are equally hateful to God
speaker: The wisdom writer
note: 14:8 curses idol and maker; 14:9–10 generalize that the deed is punished together with the doer.

title: Idolatrous rites harden into law and rulers command image worship
speaker: a grieving father, then rulers
note: Generic reported decrees in the account of idolatry's origin (cf. Hosea 13:2 record); include only if such reports count.

title: Idol worship is the beginning, cause and end of every evil
speaker: The wisdom writer
note: Same maxim at 14:12 (beginning of sexual immorality); vice list 14:22–26 shows its fruit; link as Additional Scripture.

title: Justice pursues false oaths, whatever one swears by
speaker: The wisdom writer
note: Maxim on perjury: punishment comes from justice, not from the gods sworn by; cf. Leviticus 19:12 (C0604).

title: Do not sin, knowing you are counted as God's own
speaker: The wisdom writer, addressing God
note: Confession in prayer form stating a resolve and a maxim: to know God is complete righteousness.

title: Do not treat life as a fair for gain from evil
speaker: The wisdom writer
note: Condemns the idol-maker's maxim that one must make gain from any source, even evil, knowing it is sin.

title: God's word, not herb or poultice, heals
speaker: The wisdom writer, addressing God
recipient: God; His children as the learners
note: Same teaching as 16:26 (God's utterance, not natural means, preserves); cf. 16:7. Link as Additional Scripture.

title: Give thanks before sunrise; the ungrateful person's hope melts away
speaker: The wisdom writer
note: 16:29 is the reason clause of 16:28's maxim; 16:27 gives the manna image it draws on.

title: Wickedness is cowardly, condemned by its own conscience
speaker: The wisdom writer
note: General maxims on conscience and fear drawn from the plague of darkness; cf. Proverbs 28:1.

title: Israel at the Passover pledges to share blessings and dangers alike
speaker: the holy children of Israel
recipient: one another, the people of Israel
note: Communal pact reported in the Passover retelling ('established the divine law'); not in Exodus 12. Include only if such pledges count.

title: Hatred and enslavement of strangers bring just punishment
speaker: The wisdom writer
note: Moral judgment in the retelling: Egypt's enslaving of its guests is judged worse than Sodom's inhospitality.

title: All wisdom comes from the Lord, created before all things
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Opening thesis; largely doctrine with rhetorical questions (1:2–3). Include if the book's thesis should be recorded.

title: The Lord gives wisdom to those who love Him
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 1:10b states the maxim; cf. Proverbs 2:6. Verses 1:5 and 1:7 are absent from this text.

title: Fearing the Lord brings gladness, long life and a blessed end
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Fear of the Lord is wisdom's beginning, fullness, crown and root
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Same maxim as Job 28:28 (also Proverbs 1:7, which lacks a record); a separate Sirach record would also be reasonable.

title: Unjust anger cannot be justified; its weight brings a person down
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 1:21 is absent from this text.

title: Be patient and hold back your words until the right time
speaker: Ben Sira

title: If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Direct imperative (1:26) with its grounds; nothing in Sirach 1:1–27 is recorded yet.

title: Cling to God and endure, as gold is tested in fire
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 2:5 is the reason clause of 2:4.

title: Remember how God answered those who trusted Him, for He is merciful
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 2:11 grounds 2:10: the Lord is compassionate, forgives sins and saves.

title: Woe to faint hearts, the double-minded and those who lose endurance
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Three woes; cf. James 1:8.

title: Those who fear the Lord keep His ways and humble themselves
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Declarative sayings defining the God-fearer; cf. John 14:15.

title: Listen to your father, for the Lord gave parents honor
speaker: Ben Sira
topic: Marriage, family and care for parents
note: 3:2 gives the reason for 3:1 and opens the section on honoring parents.

title: Honoring father and mother atones for sins and brings blessing
speaker: Ben Sira
topic: Marriage, family and care for parents
note: Rewards of honoring parents (atonement, answered prayer, long life); 3:6 runs into 3:7; cf. Exodus 20:12.

title: Honor your father in word and deed to receive his blessing
speaker: Ben Sira
topic: Marriage, family and care for parents
note: 3:9 is the reason clause of 3:8.

title: Do not take pride in a parent's disgrace
speaker: Ben Sira
topic: Marriage, family and care for parents
note: 3:11 is the reason clause of 3:10.

title: Support your father patiently in old age; such mercy atones
speaker: Ben Sira
topic: Marriage, family and care for parents
note: 3:14–15 give the reason: kindness to a father is credited against sins.

title: Abandoning a father is like blasphemy; angering a mother brings a curse
speaker: Ben Sira
topic: Marriage, family and care for parents

title: Stay humble as you grow, for the humble glorify the Lord
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 3:20 is the reason clause of 3:18; 3:19 is absent from this text.

title: A stubborn, proud heart ends in harm beyond healing
speaker: Ben Sira

title: A wise heart ponders proverbs and longs for a listening ear
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Almsgiving atones for sins as water quenches fire
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Cf. Daniel 4:27 (ot-daniel-v4-27).

title: Repay favors; it secures support for your own time of need
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Do not neglect the poor, lest their Maker hear their curse
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 4:6 is the reason clause of 4:5.

title: Love and seek wisdom, for the Lord loves those who love her
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Obey and trust wisdom, and she becomes your lasting inheritance
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Wisdom tests with discipline before revealing her secrets
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Includes the warning that she abandons one who goes astray (4:19).

title: Watch for the right time and know which shame to avoid
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 4:21 explains 4:20's call not to be ashamed: one shame brings sin, another glory.

title: Do not defer to others or withhold a needed word
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 4:24 is the reason clause of 4:23: wisdom is known through speech.

title: Be quick to listen, and answer only when you understand
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 5:11 sits only in the broad wealth record ot-sirach-v5-1 (5:1–11); cf. James 1:19 (A032).

title: Do not let pride tear you apart and wither you
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 6:3–4 complete the warning of 6:2: an evil soul destroys its owner.

title: Seek instruction from youth and cultivate wisdom like a farmer
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Wisdom is harsh to the undisciplined; the fainthearted abandon her
speaker: Ben Sira

title: In the end wisdom's yoke becomes rest, shelter and glory
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Promised outcome of 6:24–27 (ot-sirach-v6-24); extending that record instead would exceed four verses.

title: Wisdom grows through a willingness to listen and learn
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 6:33 is the parallel line to 6:32.

title: A leader shows wisdom by his speech; the rash talker is hated
speaker: Ben Sira

title: A wise ruler orders his people; an uninstructed king destroys them
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Rule and prosperity lie in the Lord's hand
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Pride and injustice are hateful and bring down kingdoms
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Dust and ashes have no ground for pride; kings die tomorrow
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Pride begins when the heart departs from its Maker
speaker: Ben Sira

title: The Lord overthrows proud rulers and nations and plants the humble
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Declarative examples of God humbling the proud (cf. Luke 1:52), serving the warning against pride.

title: Pride and fierce anger were not made for mortals
speaker: Ben Sira

title: True honor belongs to those who fear the Lord
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Do not dishonor the wise poor or glorify a sinful man
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 10:22 and 10:24: the boast of rich and poor alike is fearing the Lord; 10:21 is absent.

title: Free people serve a wise slave; the knowledgeable do not grumble
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Work diligently rather than boast while lacking bread
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 10:27 is the better-than saying grounding 10:26; cf. Proverbs 12:9.

title: Honor yourself with gentleness; no one honors the self-destroyer
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 10:29 is the reason clause of 10:28.

title: Honor earned by knowledge in poverty grows greater with wealth
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Do not judge by appearance; humble wisdom will be exalted
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 11:1 (the humble person's wisdom exalts him) and 11:3 (the small bee's sweet product) frame 11:2.

title: Do not boast in clothes or status; fortunes are reversed
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 11:5–6 illustrate 11:4: rulers brought low, the unsuspected crowned.

title: The Lord can raise the weak while frantic toilers stay in want
speaker: Ben Sira

title: All fortunes come from the Lord; His gift stays with the godly
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 11:15–16 are absent from this text; the reference covers 11:14 and 11:17.

title: Wealth gathered for ease may pass to others at sudden death
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Background to the rich fool (Luke 12:16–21; only Luke 12:15 is recorded, K076).

title: Trust God and keep working; He blesses the godly swiftly
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 11:22 completes the reason given in 11:21.

title: Do not assume present ease will last
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 11:25 grounds 11:23–24: good days forget the bad, and bad days the good.

title: Call no one happy before death, when the Lord repays each
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 11:26–27 lead into 11:28: at death the Lord repays and a person's works are revealed.

title: Be discerning whom you bring home; the proud lie in wait
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 11:30–32 elaborate 11:29's warning about the ambushes of the deceitful.

title: Lodging a stranger can upset your household and estrange your kin
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Restates the 11:29 caution about whom to take into your house; 11:33 intervenes, so link rather than extend.

title: Support the humble, not the ungodly, whom the Most High repays
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 12:6 is the reason clause of 12:4–5.

title: Adversity, not prosperity, reveals true friends and enemies
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Restates 6:8–10 (friends who fail in trouble); 12:8b also opens the warning about enemies in 12:10–12.

title: Never trust an enemy, even when he humbles himself
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 12:10 begins the copper-and-mirror image that 12:11 completes.

title: No one pities those entangled through keeping company with sinners
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 12:15 adds that such a companion fails you when you falter.

title: An enemy's sweet lips and tears hide murderous plans
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Whoever touches pitch is stained; associating with the proud corrupts
speaker: Ben Sira

title: The rich wrong others and threaten, while the wronged poor must plead
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Elaborates 13:2's warning about the rich and powerful.

title: The rich exploit you while useful, then mock and abandon you
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Elaborates 13:2; could instead extend ot-sirach-v13-2.

title: Beware the powerful who cannot keep words to themselves
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 13:12 is the reason for the watchfulness of 13:13; 13:14 is absent from this text.

title: Like keeps company with like; sinners have no fellowship with the godly
speaker: Ben Sira

title: The rich prey upon the poor and despise them
speaker: Ben Sira

title: The world props up the rich and dismisses the wise poor
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Wealth is good only when free from sin
speaker: Ben Sira

title: The face reflects the heart, for good or evil
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Happy is the one with a guarded tongue and a clear conscience
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Two beatitudes.

title: Wealth does a miser no good; strangers will enjoy his hoard
speaker: Ben Sira

title: No one is worse than the person who begrudges himself
speaker: Ben Sira

title: A greedy, grudging eye is never satisfied and dries up the soul
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Leads into 14:11 (ot-sirach-v14-11).

title: Remember death and do good now; your labors pass to heirs
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 14:15 is the reason for 14:14 and 14:16: your toil will be divided among heirs.

title: All flesh wears out like a garment; every generation passes away
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Mortality sayings grounding 14:16 (give and receive while you live); cites Genesis 2:17.

title: Happy is the one who meditates on wisdom and her ways
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Beatitude opening the unit that 14:22 continues.

title: Pursue wisdom like a tracker and lodge close beside her
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 14:23–24 continue the image of 14:22: peering through her windows, pitching a tent by her walls.

title: Whoever dwells beside wisdom finds shelter for himself and his children
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Whoever fears the Lord and holds to the law will gain wisdom
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Wisdom upholds and exalts those who hold to her
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Fools, sinners, the proud and liars never attain wisdom
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Praise does not befit a sinner's mouth
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Do not blame God for sin, for He hates every abomination
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 15:13 continues the reasons of 15:11–12.

title: You are free to keep the commandments; choose between life and death
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Teaching on free choice; echoes Deuteronomy 30:15–19 (C1212) but stresses responsibility, not the command itself.

title: God commands no one to sin and gives no one license
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Concludes the argument begun in 15:11; 15:18–19 add that God sees every deed.

title: Prefer one godly child to many ungodly ones
speaker: Ben Sira
topic: Marriage, family and care for parents
note: 16:4 is the reason clause of 16:3: one person of understanding settles a city.

title: Wrath is kindled against an assembly of sinners and a disobedient nation
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 16:7–10 list examples (giants, Sodom, Canaanites, wilderness generation); link as context.

title: God's mercy and rebuke are great; each is judged by deeds
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Cf. Romans 2:6 (broad record AUD-49-2-1); 16:14 adds that every act of almsgiving is rewarded.

title: Do not imagine you can hide from God, who shakes creation
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 16:18–19 answer the thought of 16:17: heaven and earth tremble at His visitation.

title: Only the senseless think God's judgment is far off
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 16:20–22 voice the fool's reasoning, judged in 16:23; 16:15–16 are absent from this text.

title: Listen and take knowledge to heart, taught with precision
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 16:25 completes the call of 16:24; 16:26–30 are a creation hymn, out of scope.

title: Humankind was given authority over the earth and its creatures
speaker: God, recalled by Ben Sira
topic: Creation, personal commissions and Israel’s journeys
note: Recalls the dominion charge of Genesis 1:28; the rest of 17:1–10 describes creation and needs no record.

title: God gives the law of life and forbids every injustice
speaker: God, recounted by Ben Sira
note: 17:11–13 recount the giving of the law and covenant that frames the charge in 17:14.

title: No human deed or sin is hidden from the Lord
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Restates 16:17: nothing is hidden from God's eyes; 17:15 says the same and could be linked too.

title: God treasures almsgiving like a signet and kindness like an eye
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Maxim inside a doctrinal passage; 17:21 is absent from this text.

title: Return to God, who opens a way back to the penitent
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 17:24 introduces the call of 17:25.

title: Return to the Most High and praise Him while you live
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 17:27–29 give the reasons: the dead cannot praise, and His mercy to those who return is great.

title: Mortals are earth and ashes, frail and prone to evil
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Observation on human frailty supporting the call to return; borderline doctrine.

title: A lifetime is a drop in the sea beside eternity
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Saying on the brevity of life; 18:11–12 apply it to God's patience. 18:1–7 are praise, out of scope.

title: The Lord shepherds all flesh with discipline; receive it
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Same teaching as Proverbs 3:11–12: the Lord shows mercy to those who accept His discipline.

title: Do not spoil a gift with reproach; a kind word surpasses it
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 18:16–18 develop 18:15: a word is better than a gift, and a fool's gift wounds.

title: A wise person is cautious in everything and guards against sin
speaker: Ben Sira

title: The understanding recognize wisdom and pour out apt proverbs
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Drunkenness impoverishes; despise small things and you fall by degrees
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Wine and prostitutes lead even the understanding astray
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Whoever trusts too quickly is shallow; sinning wrongs oneself
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Hate gossip and do not repeat what was said in confidence
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 19:5 is the first half of the sentence ending in 19:6; with 19:9 (P01822) the record becomes 19:5–9.

title: Do not repeat what was said in confidence
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 19:9 is the reason clause of 19:8; combine with the 19:5 extension (P01821) as 19:5–9.

title: Let a report die with you; only a fool must blurt it
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 19:11–12 contrast the fool who labors to release a word.

title: True wisdom is fearing the Lord, not clever wickedness
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Cf. Job 28:28 (AUD-20-28-28); 19:21 is absent, so the cluster is four verses.

title: Beware the deceiver who feigns humility to get ahead of you
speaker: Ben Sira

title: A person's bearing and look reveal his character
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Rebuke rather than nurse anger; admitting fault prevents loss
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Justice enforced by violence is as futile as a eunuch's lust
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Keep silent until the right time; babblers are loathed
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Gain may bring loss, and a bargain may cost sevenfold
speaker: Ben Sira

title: The wise win welcome by their words; fools' favors are wasted
speaker: Ben Sira

title: A fool's grudging, reproachful gift wins neither friends nor thanks
speaker: Ben Sira

title: A slip of the tongue is worse than a fall
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 20:19–20 add that untimely speech, even a proverb from a fool, is rejected.

title: Want can keep a person from sin, leaving him without remorse
speaker: Ben Sira

title: False shame can ruin a soul and turn friends into enemies
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Lying is a foul blot, worse than theft
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Wise words bring advancement and favor with the great
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 20:28b: pleasing rulers can atone for injustice.

title: God appointed rulers for the nations but kept Israel as His own
speaker: God, recounted by Ben Sira
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Echoes Deuteronomy 32:8–9 (broad context record only); include only if recalled appointments count. 17:16 and 17:18 are absent.

title: Flee sin like a snake; its wound cannot be healed
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 21:3 continues the images of 21:2: lawlessness is a two-edged sword.

title: Violence and arrogance lay waste the proud man's house
speaker: Ben Sira

title: God hears the poor man's plea and judges swiftly
speaker: Ben Sira
topic: The Little Ones and the Poor

title: The eloquent are known afar, but the wise know their own slips
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Do not build your house with other people's money
speaker: Ben Sira

title: The sinners' smooth road ends in the pit of Hades
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Keeping the law masters thought; wisdom completes the fear of the Lord
speaker: Ben Sira

title: The wise man's knowledge overflows; the fool retains none
speaker: Ben Sira

title: The wise welcome a wise word; fools cast it away
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Instruction fetters the fool but adorns the prudent
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 21:20 adds that the fool laughs loudly while the shrewd barely smile.

title: Do not barge into, peer into, or eavesdrop at a house
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Weigh your words; fools' hearts are in their mouths
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Cursing and whispering defile the speaker's own soul
speaker: Ben Sira

title: The lazy person is held in contempt like filth
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Undisciplined children and shameless daughters bring their parents shame
speaker: Ben Sira
topic: Marriage, family and care for parents
note: Ancient household view recorded as given; 22:4 commends a prudent daughter.

title: Speech out of season jars, but discipline is always wise
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Teaching a fool is like gluing potsherds together
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 22:7–8 are absent from this text.

title: Mourn the fool's lost understanding more than the dead
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 22:12 completes 22:11: mourning for the dead lasts seven days, for a fool all his life.

title: Avoid needless argument with a fool, who is heavier than lead
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 22:14–15 give the reason for 22:13.

title: A heart grounded in sound counsel will not give way to fear
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Reproach drives a friend away as stones scatter birds
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Anticipates 22:22 (ot-sirach-v22-22), where reproach is among the wrongs that end friendship.

title: Insults come before bloodshed, as smoke before fire
speaker: Ben Sira
topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours

title: Do not be ashamed to shelter a friend
speaker: Ben Sira
note: First-person resolve modelling 22:23's loyalty in trouble; 22:24 intervenes. 22:27 opens a prayer (out of scope).

title: Learn to control your speech; sinners are caught by their lips
speaker: Ben Sira
note: 23:8 is the reason clause of 23:7; the prayer in 23:1–6 is out of scope.

title: Do not make a habit of swearing oaths
speaker: Ben Sira

title: A warning against deadly and abusive speech among God's people
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Burning passion and sexual immorality never stop until they consume
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Numerical saying.

title: The adulterer who thinks no one sees forgets the Lord's eyes
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Cf. Proverbs 7:24–25 (ot-proverbs-v7-24) and Exodus 20:14.

title: A wife's adultery breaks God's law and wrongs her husband
speaker: Ben Sira

title: The adulteress faces public judgment and leaves a cursed memory
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Consequences of 23:22–23; may be merged with it (five verses).

title: Nothing is better than fearing the Lord and keeping His commandments
speaker: Ben Sira

title: Come to wisdom and eat; her fruit is sweeter than honey
speaker: personified Wisdom, in Ben Sira's poem
note: 24:17 names the fruit offered in 24:19; 24:20–21 give the reasons. 24:18 is absent.

title: The law Moses commanded overflows with wisdom like great rivers
speaker: Ben Sira

title: No one, first or last, has fully fathomed wisdom
speaker: Ben Sira

title: The teacher labored not for himself alone but for all seekers
speaker: Ben Sira
note: Same saying as 33:18. 24:30–33 are autobiography and 24:1–17 poetry (24:8 has a context record).

summary: Sirach 1-24 is thinly itemized: 162 Sirach findings (111 new sayings, most others motive clauses extending existing records); Wisdom 8-19 yields 21, mainly maxims, with the Exodus and idolatry retelling left out.
